description: An introduction to nutrition in green plants, covering photosynthesis, its raw materials and products, the structure and adaptations of the leaf, the starch test, mineral requirements and the difference between autotrophic and heterotrophic nutrition.

mcq.questionText: The process by which green plants make their own food using sunlight is called:
mcq.explanation: Photo means light and synthesis means making, so photosynthesis is the making of food using light. Exam Tip: Photosynthesis MAKES food (stores energy); respiration BREAKS food (releases energy).

mcq.questionText: The raw materials required for photosynthesis are:
mcq.explanation: The equation is carbon dioxide plus water gives glucose plus oxygen, and the inputs are on the left. Exam Tip: A and D list the PRODUCTS. Raw materials go IN; products come OUT.

mcq.questionText: The main products of photosynthesis are:
mcq.explanation: The outputs of photosynthesis are glucose, which is food, and oxygen. Exam Tip: The glucose is often stored as starch. Oxygen is a by-product released to the air.

mcq.questionText: Two conditions necessary for photosynthesis to take place are:
mcq.explanation: Photosynthesis needs light energy that is trapped by chlorophyll. Exam Tip: The four requirements are carbon dioxide, water, light and chlorophyll. Light and chlorophyll are the CONDITIONS; carbon dioxide and water are the raw materials.

mcq.questionText: In which part of the leaf does most photosynthesis take place?
mcq.explanation: The palisade layer, just below the upper surface, is packed with chloroplasts. Exam Tip: Palisade cells are column-shaped, tightly packed and near the top to catch maximum light.

mcq.questionText: The tiny pores on the surface of a leaf through which gases enter and leave are called:
mcq.explanation: Stomata are the leaf pores used for gaseous exchange and water loss. Exam Tip: A single pore is a stoma; many are stomata. They are opened and closed by guard cells.

mcq.questionText: The cells that control the opening and closing of the stomata are:
mcq.explanation: A pair of guard cells around each stoma swells or shrinks to open or close it. Exam Tip: Guard cells are the only epidermal cells with chloroplasts.

mcq.questionText: The chemical test used to show that starch is present in a leaf uses:
mcq.explanation: Iodine solution turns blue-black in the presence of starch. Exam Tip: Iodine plus starch gives blue-black; Benedict's tests reducing sugar; limewater tests carbon dioxide.

mcq.questionText: Before testing a leaf for starch, it is boiled in ethanol (alcohol) in order to:
mcq.explanation: Boiling in ethanol dissolves out the chlorophyll, leaving a pale leaf so the iodine colour shows clearly. Exam Tip: Order: boil in water, boil in ethanol (remove chlorophyll), warm water, add iodine.

mcq.questionText: Which gas is taken IN by a leaf during photosynthesis?
mcq.explanation: Carbon dioxide enters the leaf through the stomata. Exam Tip: In photosynthesis carbon dioxide goes in and oxygen comes out. In respiration the reverse happens.

mcq.questionText: The mineral element needed by plants mainly for making proteins and healthy leaf growth is:
mcq.explanation: Proteins contain nitrogen, and it gives plants lush green leaves. Exam Tip: Nitrogen deficiency leads to yellow, stunted leaves.

mcq.questionText: A plant grown in soil lacking nitrogen is likely to show:

options.text: Yellowing of leaves and stunted growth

mcq.explanation: Without nitrogen the leaves yellow and growth is poor. Exam Tip: Nitrogen deficiency gives yellow stunted leaves; magnesium deficiency gives yellowing between the veins.

mcq.questionText: The mineral element that forms part of the chlorophyll molecule is:
mcq.explanation: Magnesium is part of the chlorophyll molecule. Exam Tip: No magnesium means little chlorophyll and yellow leaves (chlorosis). Iron is needed for chlorophyll FORMATION but is not part of the molecule.

mcq.questionText: Which feature of a leaf increases the surface area for absorbing sunlight?
mcq.explanation: The broad, flat lamina, or blade, maximises light absorption. Exam Tip: Leaf adaptations include a broad lamina (light), thinness (short diffusion), many stomata (gas exchange) and veins (transport).

mcq.questionText: The type of nutrition in which organisms make their own food from simple inorganic substances is called:
mcq.explanation: Auto means self and trophic means feeding, so self-feeding is autotrophic. Exam Tip: Plants are autotrophs; animals are heterotrophs.

fib.questionText: The word equation for photosynthesis is: carbon dioxide + water → __________ + oxygen.
fib.explanation: Glucose is the food product formed alongside oxygen. Exam Tip: Learn the full equation with light and chlorophyll as conditions.

fib.questionText: The green pigment that traps light energy for photosynthesis is __________.
fib.explanation: Chlorophyll is the green pigment that absorbs light energy. Exam Tip: Chlorophyll (pigment) is inside the chloroplast (organelle).

fib.questionText: The pores on the leaf surface through which carbon dioxide enters are called __________.
fib.explanation: Stomata are the pores that allow carbon dioxide in and gases out. Exam Tip: Most stomata are on the LOWER surface, reducing water loss.

fib.questionText: The food made during photosynthesis is stored in the leaf in the form of __________.
fib.explanation: Glucose is converted to insoluble starch for storage in the leaf. Exam Tip: Starch is insoluble and tested with iodine.

fib.questionText: Testing a leaf with iodine solution gives a __________ colour when starch is present.
fib.explanation: Iodine reacts with starch to give a blue-black colour. Exam Tip: No starch means iodine stays brown/yellow.

fib.questionText: The type of nutrition shown by green plants is __________ nutrition.
fib.explanation: Green plants make their own food, which is autotrophic nutrition. Exam Tip: Animals show heterotrophic nutrition.

fib.questionText: The mineral element needed by plants for the formation of proteins is __________.
fib.explanation: Nitrogen is a key element in proteins and leaf growth. Exam Tip: Nitrogen gives proteins and leaf growth.

fib.questionText: The flat, broad part of the leaf where photosynthesis mainly occurs is called the __________.
fib.explanation: The lamina is the broad blade of the leaf where most photosynthesis happens. Exam Tip: The lamina's large flat area catches light.

fib.questionText: During photosynthesis, the gas released into the atmosphere is __________.
fib.explanation: Oxygen is the by-product released during photosynthesis. Exam Tip: This released oxygen makes the atmosphere breathable.

fib.questionText: Boiling a leaf in ethanol during the starch test removes the __________ from the leaf.
fib.explanation: Ethanol dissolves and removes the chlorophyll so the iodine colour shows clearly. Exam Tip: Ethanol is flammable, so it is heated in a water bath, not over a flame.

tf.questionText: Photosynthesis takes place only in the presence of light.
tf.explanation: In darkness no light energy is trapped, so no food is made. Exam Tip: In darkness, no light energy is trapped, so no food is made.

tf.questionText: Oxygen is one of the raw materials of photosynthesis.
tf.explanation: Oxygen is a product of photosynthesis, not a raw material. Exam Tip: Oxygen is a PRODUCT. It IS a raw material in respiration.

tf.questionText: Chlorophyll is necessary for photosynthesis because it traps light energy.
tf.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs the light energy that drives photosynthesis. Exam Tip: A variegated leaf makes starch only in the green parts.

tf.questionText: Most of the stomata are usually found on the upper surface of the leaf.
tf.explanation: Most stomata are on the lower surface where there is less heat and evaporation. Exam Tip: Stomata are mostly on the LOWER surface to reduce water loss.

tf.questionText: Starch gives a blue-black colour with iodine solution.
tf.explanation: Iodine reacts with starch to produce a blue-black colour. Exam Tip: Starch gives blue-black with iodine; reducing sugar gives brick-red with Benedict's.

tf.questionText: Green plants carry out heterotrophic nutrition.
tf.explanation: Green plants make their own food, so their nutrition is autotrophic. Exam Tip: Green plants make their own food = AUTOTROPHIC.

tf.questionText: Magnesium is needed by plants for the formation of chlorophyll.
tf.explanation: Magnesium is part of the chlorophyll molecule and is needed to form it. Exam Tip: Magnesium deficiency gives yellowing between leaf veins.

tf.questionText: During photosynthesis, plants release carbon dioxide into the air.
tf.explanation: Photosynthesis takes in carbon dioxide and releases oxygen. Exam Tip: Photosynthesis releases oxygen; carbon dioxide is released during respiration.

tf.questionText: The broad, flat shape of a leaf increases the surface area for absorbing light.
tf.explanation: A broad, flat lamina exposes more surface to sunlight. Exam Tip: Broad and flat means more light; thin means gases diffuse quickly.

tf.questionText: Photosynthesis and respiration are the same process.
tf.explanation: Photosynthesis makes food and stores energy, while respiration breaks food and releases energy. Exam Tip: They are opposite processes.

summary.correctAnswer: The process by which green plants make their own food from carbon dioxide and water using light energy trapped by chlorophyll.
summary.explanation: It stores light energy as chemical energy in glucose. Exam Tip: Photosynthesis makes food; respiration breaks food to release energy.

summary.correctAnswer: carbon dioxide + water gives glucose + oxygen, with light and chlorophyll as conditions.
summary.explanation: The raw materials are on the left and the products are on the right. Exam Tip: Write light and chlorophyll above the arrow as conditions, not raw materials.

summary.correctAnswer: Carbon dioxide and water, the substances taken in and used to make food.
summary.explanation: Carbon dioxide enters through the stomata and water comes from the roots. Exam Tip: Raw materials go IN; products come OUT.

summary.correctAnswer: Glucose, which is food, and oxygen, which is released as a by-product.
summary.explanation: Glucose is often stored as starch and oxygen is released to the air. Exam Tip: Do not confuse the products with the raw materials.

summary.correctAnswer: The green pigment inside chloroplasts that traps light energy for photosynthesis.
summary.explanation: Without chlorophyll a plant cannot absorb light to make food. Exam Tip: Chlorophyll is the pigment; the chloroplast is the organelle that holds it.

summary.correctAnswer: Tiny pores on the leaf surface through which gases enter and leave and water vapour escapes.
summary.explanation: They allow carbon dioxide in and oxygen out during photosynthesis. Exam Tip: One pore is a stoma; many are stomata, mostly on the lower surface.

summary.correctAnswer: A pair of cells around each stoma that swell or shrink to open or close the pore.
summary.explanation: They control gas exchange and water loss by opening and closing the stomata. Exam Tip: Guard cells are the only epidermal cells with chloroplasts.

summary.correctAnswer: A test in which a decolourised leaf is treated with iodine solution, turning blue-black if starch is present.
summary.explanation: The leaf is boiled in water, then in ethanol to remove chlorophyll, before adding iodine. Exam Tip: Ethanol is flammable, so heat it in a water bath, not over a flame.

summary.correctAnswer: Autotrophic nutrition is making your own food from simple inorganic substances, while heterotrophic nutrition is feeding on ready-made organic food from other organisms.
summary.explanation: Green plants are autotrophs and animals are heterotrophs. Exam Tip: Auto means self-feeding; hetero means feeding on others.

summary.correctAnswer: Nitrogen is needed to make proteins and healthy green leaves, while magnesium is part of the chlorophyll molecule.
summary.explanation: Lack of nitrogen gives yellow stunted leaves; lack of magnesium gives yellowing between the veins. Exam Tip: Iron is needed for chlorophyll formation but is not part of the molecule.

hoq.questionText: A destarched plant with variegated leaves (green and white patches) is left in bright sunlight for six hours. A leaf is then tested for starch with iodine. What result is expected, and what does it prove?

options.text: The whole leaf turns blue-black; proves water is needed
Only the green parts turn blue-black; proves chlorophyll is needed for photosynthesis
Only the white parts turn blue-black; proves light is not needed
No part turns blue-black; proves starch is not made in leaves

hoq.explanation: Chlorophyll is present only in the green parts, so starch is made only there. Iodine turns those parts blue-black while the white parts stay brown. Exam Tip: The variable tested is CHLOROPHYLL (green vs white), so the conclusion must be about chlorophyll.

hoq.questionText: A student set up pondweed in water and counted bubbles of gas per minute at different distances from a lamp: 10 cm gave 60 bubbles, 20 cm gave 30 bubbles, 30 cm gave 15 bubbles. What does the gas released indicate, and what is the relationship shown?

options.text: The gas is carbon dioxide; more light means fewer bubbles
The gas is oxygen; the rate of photosynthesis increases as the lamp gets closer (more light)
The gas is oxygen; light has no effect on the rate
The gas is nitrogen; distance has no effect

hoq.explanation: The gas is oxygen. As the lamp moves closer, more light reaches the plant and more bubbles rise, so the rate of photosynthesis increases with light intensity. Exam Tip: Counting bubbles measures the RATE; the bubbles are oxygen. A nearer lamp gives brighter light and a faster rate.

hoq.questionText: Two identical plants were grown for four weeks. Plant A received a complete mineral solution; Plant B received the same solution but with nitrogen removed. Plant B became yellow and stunted while Plant A stayed green and healthy. Which conclusion is valid?

options.text: Nitrogen is needed for healthy growth and green leaves
Water is the cause of yellowing
Light was missing from Plant B
Plant B had too much nitrogen

hoq.explanation: The only difference was nitrogen. Plant B without nitrogen yellowed and was stunted, while Plant A with nitrogen was healthy, so nitrogen is needed for healthy growth and green leaves. Exam Tip: In a fair test only ONE variable changes. B and C name controlled factors; D contradicts the data.
